assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Each policy threshold (650 for non-seniors, 600 for seniors) is verifiable from the table via boundary rows or a policy column.
assertions.evidence: Rows: '650 | true | REJECTED' vs '651 | true | APPROVED'; '600...REJECTED' vs '601...APPROVED'

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms, not abstract codes.
assertions.evidence: '40 | 650 | true | REJECTED', '70 | 601 | true | APPROVED' — concrete ages, scores, decisions

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Just above the standard threshold', 'Senior age boundary, lower threshold applies' — condition-based names

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language.
assertions.evidence: 'Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Result?' — all business terms, no code identifiers

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are each covered without a monolithic cross-multiplied table.
assertions.evidence: Single table with rows split by concern (age/credit boundaries rows1-6, income rows7-11), no full cross-product

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed, no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: Row 9 'Senior qualifying score with missing income information' redundantly re-tests pending rule across age; row10's {true,false} value set duplicates row1's true+below-threshold case

assertions.text: Age boundary, credit categorisation, and income status each covered by minimal scenarios.
assertions.evidence: Age/credit via rows1-6 boundary pairs; income via rows7-11 varying Stable Income

assertions.text: Scenario names/@Description do not restate values the table already shows.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'credit score of 650...lower threshold of 600...senior age cutoff is inclusive at 65' — values literally present as row cells (650, 600, 65)

assertions.text: Stable income's effect is visible via a held-constant row pair.
assertions.evidence: Rows 'Qualifying score with unstable income | 40 | 700 | false | REJECTED' vs '...missing income information | 40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW' — same age/score, differing income and decision

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Result column varies across REJECTED/APPROVED/PENDING_REVIEW depending on inputs, not a fixed or copied value

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Boundary rows like '650|REJECTED' and '651|APPROVED', '600|REJECTED' and '601|APPROVED', and age pair '64,610|REJECTED' vs '65,610|APPROVED' let a reader infer both thresholds and age cutoff from cell values alone.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does, not an external fact.
assertions.evidence: void evaluatesLoanApproval(...) — the fallback name describes the evaluator's action, not a restated regulation or domain fact.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule depends on and held constant for every row must be visible as a column or named in title/description.
assertions.evidence: All rule-relevant inputs (Age, Credit Score, Stable Income) vary across rows and are explicit columns; no hidden constant (e.g., currency, region) is fixed silently in the method body or a field.
